<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **17** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-docusign/objectstack.manifest.json`, `packages/apps/connector-github/objectstack.manifest.json`, `packages/apps/connector-stripe/objectstack.manifest.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **181** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d612225a19facf86f8151be852edb74705d31764` — the merge of head `5da9dd3c992a8eebf258e58c3c74543dad86853f` into base `cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d612225a19facf86f8151be852edb74705d31764 && git checkout d612225a19facf86f8151be852edb74705d31764
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7 5da9dd3c992a8eebf258e58c3c74543dad86853f && git checkout -B drift-repro cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7 && git merge --no-ff 5da9dd3c992a8eebf258e58c3c74543dad86853f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cad764d3e2d71210bce48653aa823a3b940071d7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `31035-template-manifest-inert-keys-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/cli` minor, `create-objectstack` patch. Under ruling A as the gate reads it (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: a declared kind must grade at least one moved package `minor` or above), `narrowed` with spec and cli at `minor` is correct; `create-objectstack` at `patch` is allowed (the protocol it publishes against is unchanged; it only stops writing refused keys). `Check Changeset` concluded success.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file judged against the `spec-property-retirement` playbook at the head, ADR-0049 / ADR-0087 as amended, the `category` precedent on the same schema (#30980), and the first consumers (`os package publish`, `check:template-manifests`, create-objectstack, the new pin).

- `packages/spec/src/marketplace/template-manifest.zod.ts` — HOLDS. Route: `retiredKey()` tombstones on a non-strict shape (a bare delete would strip silently; the schema header says so). Guidance strings follow the five house conventions: backticked fully-qualified key first (`TemplateManifest.KEY`), `was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 (ADR-0049)`, one dash clause on why it was inert, imperative fix (`Delete the key.`) plus the mechanism that actually works (`manifestId` / `package.json` name, `manifest.engines.protocol`, the whole skills catalog, nothing, `--visibility`), and no `os migrate meta` sentence because no conversion exists — identical to `retiredCategoryGuidance`; the migrate-sentence pin judges only strings carrying the marker, so none is owed. No issue number in a guidance string (`#31035` sits in comments only). The `visibility` override on an inherited live key is the one subtle piece and it is correct: `.omit().extend()` replaces the inherited field on this file only, `CreatePackageRequestSchema` is untouched, and the pin's `--visibility` control proves the flag path still sends it. Tried to break it: `"visibility": null` is refused by both the schema (`z.never`) and publish (`!== undefined`), consistent; `specVersion` was REQUIRED before, so any manifest that satisfied the old schema now fails — which is the declared BREAKING, carried by the banner and the FROM → TO list. The tsc channel is moot for a JSON file; the real author channels are the `$schema` JSON-schema projection (regenerated from the `never`), `check:template-manifests`, and publish's warning / refusal — the same channels `category` has.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.marketplace__TemplateManifest__{name,scaffold,skills,specVersion,visibility}.ts` — HOLD. Filenames derive from the ids per `shardNameFor` (`/` and `:` to `__`), entry values are the exact `authorable-surface` spellings, one file per key with its why-comment above `export const entry` (the shape build-schemas gate b matches as a set member); the comment prose names `retiredKey()` the way the `category` entry already on `main` does, so no live textual ratchet is newly matched. Registered in the same PR as the tombstones, so gate (b2) "registration with no consumer" cannot fire. The ageing clock starts at 18, as the ADR-0087 2026-10-26 amendment wants.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.marketplace-template-manifest-inert-keys-retired.ts` — HOLDS. One D3 entry per family, kebab id ending in `-retired`, `surface` as prose joined with ` / `, `replacement`, `reason` (states the D3-not-D2 ground: no seam ever loads this file; moving `visibility` to the command line is a judgement) and `acceptanceCriteria` (every claim in it is true on the tree: tsc mark, parse refusal, publish refusal for `visibility` before any network call, four shipped manifests clean, create-objectstack no longer writes `name`). It names `publisher` / `isStarter` as deliberately outside the family, which is what a reader of the upgrade guide needs.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template` — HOLDS. The `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment is inserted at its sorted position (between `marketplace-category-retired` and `memory-persistence-placeholder-refused`), `order: 120` is one more than the previous highest (119), so it renders directly after the `category` sentence, and its text ("It also retires five ...") reads correctly there. Only the template's prose was touched; `registry.ts` is generated and git-ignored.

Findings:

- must-fix: none.
- should-fix (this PR or a tight follow-up): `packages/create-objectstack/src/index.ts#rewriteProjectIdentity` deletes only `name`. A REMOTE template authored before this release still carries `specVersion`, `skills`, `scaffold` (and possibly `visibility`), and the scaffolder — which already rewrites this file and knows the retired set — hands the new project a manifest the schema refuses and publish warns on (or, for `visibility`, refuses).
